name: Reuben
overview: Reuben, the firstborn son of Jacob, is introduced as a child born to Leah who hoped his birth would secure her husband's love (Genesis 29:32). He is noted for bringing mandrakes, an aphrodisiac, to his mother during the wheat harvest (Genesis 30:14), reflecting his familial involvement. Although he showed a protective spirit by attempting to save Joseph from his brothers' deadly conspiracy (Genesis 37:21-22), Reuben's legacy is marred by his grievous sin of lying with his father's concubine, Bilhah, which led to forfeiting his birthright (Genesis 35:22). These events highlight a complex character whose actions had significant consequences within Jacob's family.
